dial.summary: DXY strengthened to 102.22 on safe-haven flows and BTC.D rose to 59.3% as Bitcoin crossed $86,500 — structural macro headwinds (real yields at 2.89%, DXY above 102) persist, but TOTAL crypto cap reached $2.92T and BTC-specific accumulation continues with near-neutral funding; stablecoin dominance ticked up to ~11.0% signaling $321B+ in sidelined capital available to deploy; FOMC minutes (Oct 7) and September CPI (Oct 14) remain the dominant catalysts for a regime shift.

indicators.name: Global Liquidity (Global M2)
indicators.note: G4 M2 aggregate (Fed/ECB/BOJ/PBOC) at ~$103.6T based on August 2026 data (latest available); component breakdown: US $23.3T, China $53.1T, Eurozone $19.1T, Japan $8.1T; September G4 M2 not yet available (6–8 week reporting lag); 4-week trend flat: no confirmed September G4 data, 3-month growth rate through August was +1.17% (normal pace); YoY still meaningfully positive (not contracting); status neutral — confirmed rising 4-week trend required for supportive; ISM Prices at 77.9% and elevated CPI present a stagflation signal complicating the liquidity expansion narrative; next G4 M2 update expected mid-November 2026.

indicators.name: ISM Manufacturing PMI
indicators.note: September 2026 ISM Manufacturing PMI = 54.5%, released October 1 (confirmed via ISM PR Newswire) — ninth consecutive month of manufacturing expansion; 4-week trend flat: August 54.6% → September 54.5% = −0.1pp, within the flat threshold; New Orders Index 55.3% (bullish forward signal); Production Index 56.7%; Prices Index 77.9% (highest since mid-2021, a leading CPI upside signal); status neutral (above 50 but flat; supportive requires above 50 AND rising); ISM Services PMI for September released October 5 (watch for services confirmation of broad expansion); next ISM Manufacturing release November 3, 2026.

indicators.name: DXY (US Dollar Index)
indicators.note: ICE DXY at ~102.22 on October 5, 2026, gathering strength on safe-haven flows with an intraday high of 102.53 — a 16-month high per Trading Economics; 4-week trend up: ~99.9 (Sep 5) → 102.22 (Oct 5) = +2.3% over 30 days, well above the 0.5% flat threshold; status headwind (above 100 threshold); DXY strength despite September NFP shock (+29K) reflects safe-haven demand and persistent USD structural bid; a sustained close below 100 required to return to neutral; October 14 CPI is the next major DXY repricing catalyst.

indicators.name: Real Yields (US10Y - CPI)
indicators.note: FRED DFII10 (10-year TIPS constant maturity) at 2.89% as of October 2, 2026 (latest Fed H.15; next update October 5 after market close); breakeven inflation rate 2.28% (stagflation premium building with ISM Prices at 77.9%); 4-week trend up: ~2.50% (Sep 3) → 2.89% (Oct 2) = +39bps over 30 days; status headwind (rising 4-week trend AND above 2% absolute threshold both met); 10Y nominal yield at 5.28% despite weak September NFP, reflecting fiscal and stagflation concerns; a sustained fall below 2% required to shift status to neutral; October 14 CPI is the next key real yield repricing catalyst.

indicators.name: 2s10s Yield Curve
indicators.note: October 2, 2026: 10Y Treasury 5.28%, 2Y Treasury 4.83% → 2s10s spread = +0.45% (+45bps); 4-week trend up (steepening): Sep 3 spread ~+42bps → Oct 2 +45bps = +3bps steepening over 30 days; status supportive (both positive AND steepening on 4-week basis); post-NFP curve steepening driven by 2Y falling faster than 10Y as Fed hold expectations rose sharply after +29K payroll miss; October 14 CPI and October 27–28 FOMC are the next major yield curve catalysts.

indicators.name: Fed Balance Sheet
indicators.note: WALCL: $6,743,031M ($6.74T) for week ending September 30, 2026 per Federal Reserve H.4.1 released October 1 (most recent; next H.4.1 release October 8 for week ending October 7); 4-week trend flat: Sep 2 $6,737,204M → Sep 30 $6,743,031M = +$5.8B marginal expansion within flat threshold on a $6.74T balance sheet; status supportive (holding at post-2022 stabilization plateau; no QT acceleration at Sep 15–16 FOMC where FFR was raised to 3.75%–4.00%); weak September NFP (+29K) raises probability of a Fed hold at October 27–28 FOMC, supportive for balance sheet stability.

indicators.name: BTC Funding Rates (perps avg)
indicators.note: BTC perpetual funding rate at approximately 0.0100% per 8h as of October 5, 2026 per CoinGlass (7DMA annualized: Binance ~6.9%, Bybit ~8.2% as of late September, translating to ~0.007–0.010% per 8h); BTC price at ~$86,500 with open interest up $2.3B (27,000 BTC) since September 30 per CoinDesk, signaling growing bullish leverage; 4-week trend up: rose from lower September levels (~0.001–0.007% range) toward 0.010% as BTC rallied; status supportive (significantly below 0.04% overheating threshold, confirming spot-driven price action); October 14 CPI and October 27–28 FOMC are next potential funding regime catalysts.

indicators.name: Stablecoin Dominance
indicators.note: Stablecoin market cap ~$321B as of October 5, 2026 (Bitcoin Foundation: 'Stablecoin Market Cap Tops $321B, Extending 2026 Growth'); total crypto market cap ~$2.92T; BTC.D 59.36%; stablecoin dominance ~11.0% (321/2920); 30-day trend up: ~10.4% (Sep 5) → 11.0% (Oct 5) = +0.6pp; status headwind (rising on 30-day basis while TOTAL crypto market cap is also rising from ~$2.89T to $2.92T, per the rules); USDT and USDC hold ~83% of stablecoin market; rising dominance alongside a rising TOTAL cap suggests capital is flowing into stablecoins faster than into risk assets, a sign of caution; October 14 CPI is the next major catalyst for stablecoin inflow/outflow dynamics.

upcoming.title: US Trade Balance (August 2026)
upcoming.note: Census Bureau Trade Balance for August 2026 at 8:30 AM ET; consensus deficit ~$95.2B; net exports are a direct Q3 GDP component — a wider-than-expected deficit would subtract from the Q3 advance estimate (October 29); provides context on whether the strong dollar (DXY 102.22) has materially weighed on US export competitiveness; released in the same week as FOMC minutes, adding to the Fed's growth-vs-inflation calculus.

upcoming.title: FOMC Minutes (September 15–16, 2026 Meeting)
upcoming.note: Federal Reserve releases minutes of the September 15–16 FOMC meeting at 2:00 PM ET — the meeting at which the Fed raised the fed funds rate 25bps to 3.75%–4.00%; minutes will reveal committee debate on further tightening pace, any dissents, and how members framed the balance between inflation (ISM Prices 77.9%, CPI ~3.5% YoY) and employment risks; critical to parse for October hold signals given the subsequent September NFP miss (+29K); market is pricing high probability of a hold at October 27–28 FOMC.

upcoming.title: Initial Jobless Claims (week ended October 4, 2026)
upcoming.note: DOL weekly initial jobless claims at 8:30 AM ET for the week ended October 4, 2026 — first claims reading fully capturing early-October labor conditions post the September NFP shock (+29K); prior weeks approximately 206K; consecutive claims above 225K would reinforce Fed hold expectations for October 27–28 and signal the NFP miss is a trend rather than a one-off; released the day after FOMC Minutes, providing a real-time follow-up to the September labor narrative.

upcoming.title: University of Michigan Consumer Sentiment (October 2026 Preliminary)
upcoming.note: University of Michigan Consumer Sentiment preliminary reading for October 2026 at 10:00 AM ET; September final was ~69.1; provides early read on consumer confidence heading into Q4 — a key forward indicator for retail sales and consumption; with DXY at 102.22, real yields at 2.89%, and the September NFP shock fresh, a weak print below 65 would reinforce risk-off tone; the 1-year and 5-year inflation expectations sub-components are closely watched by the Fed for second-round effects given ISM Prices at 77.9%.
